//: Art spec for `node tools/genimage.js`. Only the cover is listed: this Teacher's Guide places no pictures of its own in the body. The prompt says only what the picture must DEPICT; the standing requirements (semi-realistic register, Zambian setting, equal male/female, a visible disability wherever people appear, no lettering) are appended to every prompt by the tool, so they are not repeated here except where the scene needs them placed concretely.
//why: The manuscript ships no cover artwork at all — its cover page carries the bracketed instruction '[Please, put suitable cover page ]' where the picture should be. With no hero image the engine falls back to its abstract motif (a tilted panel with ellipses), which depicts nothing about the book. House style requires a cover whose pictures depict what the book is actually about, so one has to be made.
//age: Learners in this book are Grade 1 — about six to seven years old. The replacement must show children of that age, not the older primary learners a generic 'schoolchildren' prompt tends to produce.
//subject: Kiikaonde, the language itself, taught as a first language. The book's own strands are KWAMBA NE KUTELEKA (speaking and listening), KUTANGA (reading), KUNEMBA (writing), BYAMBO (vocabulary) and KUMVWISHA (comprehension), so the scene is an early-literacy lesson rather than a generic classroom. Kaonde is spoken in North-Western Zambia and the author teaches in Solwezi, so the setting should read as that part of the country. This is a Teacher's Guide, so the teacher is doing the teaching and is prominent, not incidental.
//lettering: The no-lettering rule matters more than usual here. This is a language book, and the obvious instinct — an alphabet chart, flashcards, words on a chalkboard — would put text in the picture. Every surface that would normally carry writing must be blank or purely pictorial, and the reading and writing have to be shown through posture, gesture and materials instead.
//geometry: The hero card for this cover is 144mm x 78mm (generic-template.typ:748), i.e. 1.846:1, placed with fit:"cover". (NOT the 148mm x 78mm card: that is the `flask` branch at :744, which only the Chemistry motif takes. The earlier version of this file had the wrong one.) The model returns 1536x1024 (1.5:1); resampled to 1800 across that is 1800x1200, and a centre-crop to 1800x975 gives the card's ratio, so the engine crops nothing further and no edge of the artwork is lost. 1800px across 144mm is 317 DPI, clearing the 300 DPI print requirement. The crop takes about 9% off the top and the same off the bottom, which is why the prompt insists every face and every object sits well inside the middle band.

cover.prompt: A bright, warm Zambian lower-primary classroom in North-Western Province, filling the whole frame edge to edge with no border, no vignette and no blank margin, and with every face and every object kept well inside the middle band of the picture — nothing important in the top fifth or the bottom fifth, which will be cropped away. A woman teacher sits on a low chair at the centre, leaning towards four Grade 1 pupils gathered close around her — small children of about six or seven, with rounded faces and short stature, clearly infants rather than older primary learners. Two boys and two girls. One of the boys uses a child-sized wheelchair and is drawn right up in the group with the others, leaning in towards the teacher, part of the circle rather than beside it. The children wear simple light blue school shirts and navy tunics. The lesson is early language work, shown through gesture rather than text: the teacher is mid-speech with one hand open in an explaining gesture and the children are watching her mouth and listening, one child has a hand raised ready to answer, one is holding an open picture book flat on her lap with both hands, and one is tracing a shape in the air with a finger. On a low table beside them, a stack of plain exercise books, a pot of short pencils, and three large picture cards showing only drawings — a cooking pot, a goat, a maize cob — with no words on them. Behind the group a green chalkboard bearing only simple chalk drawings of a hut, a tree and a sun, a low shelf of books, a woven basket, and an open window with mango trees and red earth outside. Warm daylight, cheerful colours, an attentive and friendly mood. Absolutely no letters, numbers, words, writing, signage or labels anywhere in the picture — the chalkboard, the picture cards, the exercise books and the book in the child's hands must all be blank or purely pictorial.
